_about: Deterministic trust scoring rules. The code reads these; no LLM decides a score.

fail_if.rule: label != case_card (only when the label comes from text/metadata/registry/human, or from the LLM with conf >= 0.9)
fail_if.reason: For PC {label}, your case is PC {case}

unknown_if.rule: null, or via llm/container with conf < 0.9

metrics.name: System agreement
metrics.flag_if_zero: The payroll engine uses {engine_value}, but this source says {value}

metrics.name: Law anchor
metrics.rule: +8 if legal_ref matches the registry rule currently valid for claim.key; +7 if reviewed_on >= registry.changed_on
metrics.flag_if_partial: The law changed on {changed_on}, after this source was last reviewed ({reviewed_on})

metrics.name: Authority and owner
metrics.rule: type points (doc 8, email 4, teams 1) + 7 if the owner is active

metrics.name: Expert endorsement
metrics.rule: 15 if confirmed by a person with >= 10 decisions in this country/PC; 8 if confirmed by another colleague; else 0

metrics.name: Outcome record
metrics.rule: times_used < 5: 0 ('not enough history'); correction rate < 2%: 15; < 10%: 8; else 0

metrics.name: Independent agreement
metrics.rule: Count other sources that pass the gate, have the same claim value and a different copy_group: >= 2 → 10, 1 → 5, 0 → 0

metrics.name: Doubt signal
metrics.rule: Teams questions in the last 90 days: 0–1 → 10, 2–4 → 5, >= 5 → 0

warnings.rule: another gate-passing source has a different claim value
warnings.effect: flag on every source involved; cap at yellow only if a contradicting source also scores >= 80

warnings.rule: translation_of is set and reviewed_on < original.reviewed_on
a critical label comes only from llm/container
